heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 內篇 明倫 102 … 小學 內篇 敬身 14

items.text: Serve them with forbearance and without harsh remonstrance; attend them constantly; labor for them until death; mourn for three years.
items.quote: 事親有隱而無犯。 左右就養無方。 服勤至死。 致喪三年。 — Serve parents with forbearance, without harsh remonstrance; attend them constantly; labor until death; mourn three years.

items.text: Because you received life from him, treat him as you treat your ruler and teacher; repay life with death and kindness with strength.
items.quote: 民生於三。 事之如一。 父生之，師敎之，君食之。 非父不生，非食不長，非敎不知。 生之族也。 故壹事之，唯其所在則致死焉。 — One is born of three and serves them alike: father begets, teacher instructs, ruler feeds. Without father no birth; without food no growth; without teaching no knowledge. So serve him unto death.

items.text: Be kind to your children and instruct them.
items.quote: 父慈而敎 — Be kind and instruct your children.

items.text: Be filial and, when necessary, admonish them gently.
items.quote: 子孝而箴 — Be filial and admonish gently.

items.text: Love your younger brother and be friendly.
items.quote: 兄愛而友 — Love and be friendly to your younger brother.

items.text: Respect your elder brother and be obedient.
items.quote: 弟敬而順 — Respect and obey your elder brother.

items.text: Be gentle with your wife.
items.quote: 夫和而義 — Be gentle and righteous to your wife.

items.text: Be gentle and submissive to your husband.
items.quote: 妻柔而正 — Be gentle and upright to your husband.

items.text: Be kind to your daughter-in-law and defer to her in non-essential matters.
items.quote: 姑慈而從 — Be kind and yielding to your daughter-in-law.

items.text: Obey your mother-in-law and be gentle.
items.quote: 婦聽而婉 — Obey and be gentle with your mother-in-law.

items.text: While they live, serve them without delay; for after death you cannot be filial.
items.quote: 親戚旣沒，雖欲孝誰爲孝。 年旣耆艾，雖欲悌誰爲悌。 故孝有不及，悌有不時 — After parents are gone, whom can you serve? After elders are aged, whom can you respect? Filial service has a season; do not delay.

items.text: Treat your own body as a branch of your parents; do not injure it, for injuring yourself harms them.
items.quote: 身也者親之枝也。 敢不敬與。 不能敬其身，是傷其親。 — Your body is a branch of your parents; dare you not revere it? To injure your body is to wound your parents.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 內篇 立教 5 … 小學 內篇 立教 13

items.text: Be affectionate with your son.
items.quote: 父子有親 — Father and son have affection.

items.text: Serve your parents well.
items.quote: 孝謂善事父母 — Filial piety means serving parents well.

items.text: Maintain proper distinction between husband and wife.
items.quote: 夫婦有別 — Husband and wife have separate spheres.

items.text: Observe the proper order between elder and younger.
items.quote: 長幼有序 — Elder and younger have their order.

items.text: Be good to your brothers and sisters.
items.quote: 友謂善於兄弟 — Friendliness means being good to brothers.

items.text: Be close to all your relatives.
items.quote: 睦謂親於九族 — Harmony means being close to all relatives.

items.text: Be close to your maternal relatives.
items.quote: 婣謂親於外親 — Affinity means being close to relatives through marriage or mother.

items.text: Be gentle and fraternal; do not be arrogant or rely on force.
items.quote: 溫柔孝弟毋驕恃力 — Be gentle, filial, fraternal; do not be arrogant or rely on force.

items.text: When serving your parents, exhaust your strength.
items.quote: 事父母能竭其力 — Serve parents with all your strength.

items.text: Help your relatives in distress and poverty.
items.quote: 卹謂振於憂貧 — Compassion means relieving those in distress and poverty.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 內篇 明倫 34 … 小學 內篇 明倫 58

items.text: Do not harm your body, for it is received from your parents; treat it with care as the beginning of filial piety.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 明倫 34
items.quote: 身體髪膚受之父母。不敢毀傷孝之始也。 — The body, hair, and skin are received from one's parents; not daring to harm them is the beginning of filial piety.

items.text: Establish yourself in the Way and make a good name for posterity, thereby bringing honor to your parents.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 明倫 34
items.quote: 立身行道，揚名於後世，以顯父母 — Establish yourself and practice the Way, make a name for later generations to glorify your parents.

items.text: Love and respect your parents, and do not hate or show disrespect to others, lest you bring shame on them.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 明倫 34
items.quote: 愛親者不敢惡於人，敬親者不敢慢於人 — One who loves his parents does not dare to hate others; one who respects his parents does not dare to be rude to others.

items.text: Work according to the seasons and land, be careful in conduct and frugal, and thus provide for your parents.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 明倫 34
items.quote: 用天之道，因地之利，謹身節用以養父母 — Follow the way of heaven, use the advantages of the land, be careful in conduct and frugal in spending to support father and mother.

items.text: Love and respect your own parents above all; do not love or respect others while neglecting them.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 明倫 35
items.quote: 不愛其親而愛他人者，謂之悖德。不敬其親而敬他人者，謂之悖禮 — Not loving one's own parents but loving others is called perverse virtue; not respecting one's own parents but respecting others is called perverse propriety.

items.text: Serve your parents with reverence in daily life, with joy in providing for them, and with concern when they are ill.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 明倫 36
items.quote: 居則致其敬，養則致其樂，病則致其憂 — In daily life show reverence, in support show joy, in illness show concern.

items.text: Mourn your parents with grief and offer sacrifices to them with reverence.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 明倫 36
items.quote: 喪則致其哀，祭則致其嚴 — In mourning show grief, in sacrifice show reverence.
items.conflict: Contrary to the first commandment: worship belongs to God alone; ancestor veneration is prohibited (Deut. 18:10-12; 1 Cor. 10:20).

items.text: In serving your parents, avoid arrogance in high position, rebellion in low position, and contentiousness among equals; these negate even lavish support.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 明倫 36
items.quote: 居上不驕，爲下不亂，在醜不爭 — not proud when high, not rebellious when low, not contentious among equals.

items.text: Do not neglect your parents' support through laziness, gambling, greed, self-indulgence, or fighting; all these are unfilial.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 明倫 37
items.quote: 惰其四支不顧父母之養，一不孝也 — idle in limbs, not caring for parents' support, is the first unfilial act.

items.text: Conduct yourself with dignity at home, loyalty to the ruler, respect in office, trustworthiness with friends, and courage in battle, because your body is your parents' legacy; failure brings disgrace to them.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 明倫 38
items.quote: 居處不莊非孝也。事君不忠非孝也。蒞官不敬非孝也。 — Unbecoming conduct at home is unfilial; disloyalty to the ruler is unfilial; irreverence in office is unfilial.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 外篇 嘉言 78 … 小學 外篇 嘉言 91

items.text: Teach your children the literary arts, so their minds are cultivated and not led astray by ambition for office.
items.quote: 父兄以文藝令其子弟 — Fathers and elder brothers make their sons and younger brothers study literary arts.

items.text: Teach your younger brothers the literary arts, so their minds are cultivated and not led astray by ambition for office.
items.quote: 父兄以文藝令其子弟 — Fathers and elder brothers make their sons and younger brothers study literary arts.

items.text: When entrusted with a letter or item for a kinsman, even one close or junior, do not keep it; see that it reaches him.
items.quote: 雖至親卑幼者，亦未嘗輒留。必爲附至。 — Even for close relatives and juniors, I never kept it; I always delivered it.

items.text: Learn from the ancients: anticipate your parents' wishes, speak gently and cheerfully, and spare no effort to provide them with nourishing food.
items.quote: 未知養親者，欲其觀古人之先意，承顏，怡聲，下氣，不憚劬勞以致甘腝 — Those who do not know how to care for parents should look at how the ancients anticipated their wishes, showed a cheerful face, spoke softly and humbly, and spared no effort to provide delicacies.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 內篇 明倫 77 … 小學 內篇 明倫 101

items.text: When drinking with an elder, do not drink before the elder has finished his cup.
items.quote: 長者舉未釂，少者不敢飮。 — When the elder has raised his cup but not finished, the younger does not dare drink.

items.text: When an elder gives you something, do not decline it.
items.quote: 長者賜，少者?賤者不敢辭。 — When an elder gives, the younger or lowly does not dare decline.

items.text: When dining with an elder, even if the food is doubled, do not decline it.
items.quote: 禦同於長者，雖貳不辭。 — When dining with an elder, even if it is doubled, do not decline.

items.text: In the presence or service of an elder, show utmost respect: do not ask their age or where they are going, do not fidget or fan yourself, kneel when delivering messages, and in games handle arrows carefully and ask permission before drinking if you win.
items.quote: 侍坐，弗使不執琴瑟，不畫地，手無容，不翣也。寢則坐而將命。 — When sitting with an elder, do not play the qin or draw unless asked, do not fidget or fan; when he is lying down, kneel to deliver messages.

items.text: On the road, yield to those of your father's or elder brother's age; combine and divide loads to help, and do not let white-haired elders carry things or walk without a carriage.
items.quote: 父之齒隨行，兄之齒鴈行，輕任幷重任分，頒白者不提挈。 — Follow those of your father's age, walk side by side with those of your elder brother's age, combine light loads and divide heavy ones, and do not let white-haired elders carry things.

items.text: At village drinking ceremonies, wait until the elders with staffs have left before you leave.
items.quote: 郷人飮酒杖者出斯出矣。 — At village drinking, only after the staff-carrying elders leave do you leave.

items.text: Serve your parents with filial piety, caring for their needs and obeying them.
items.quote: 君子之事親孝。 — The gentleman serves his parents with filial piety.

items.text: Serve your elder brother with obedience and respect.
items.quote: 事兄弟。 — Serve elder brothers.

items.text: When your father is about to do something unrighteous, remonstrate with him so he does not fall into unrighteousness.
items.quote: 父有爭子，則身不陷於不義。故當不義，則子不可以弗爭於父。 — If a father has a son who will remonstrate, he will not fall into unrighteousness; therefore when it is unrighteous, the son must not fail to remonstrate with his father.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 內篇 稽古 23 … 小學 內篇 稽古 44

items.text: Treat your spouse with the respect due a guest.
items.quote: 敬相待如賓 — respectfully treat each other as guests.

items.text: Remain chaste to your deceased husband and refuse pressure to remarry.
items.quote: 共姜守義... 以死自誓 — Gong Jiang kept her vow... swore by death.
items.conflict: Remarriage of widows is permissible (1 Cor 7:39).

items.text: Do not leave your husband when he suffers a serious illness, for you are bound for life.
items.quote: 適人之道，壹與之醮，終身不改 — The way of a married woman: once joined with him in the wedding cup, never change for life.

items.text: Do not store up anger or resentment against a younger brother, but love him.
items.quote: 仁人之於弟也不藏怒焉，不宿怨焉，親愛之而已矣 — A benevolent person does not harbor anger or keep resentment towards his younger brother; he only loves him.

items.text: Obey your father's command even after his death.
items.quote: 父命也 — It is my father's command.

items.text: Yield precedence to an elder brother rather than taking the position yourself.
items.quote: 叔齊讓伯夷 — Shu Qi yielded to Bo Yi.

items.text: Take up the burdens of elders so they do not have to carry them.
items.quote: 班白不提挈 — the gray-haired did not carry burdens.

items.text: Arrange a suitable marriage for a nephew or niece in your care.
items.quote: 孔子以其兄之子妻之 — Confucius gave his elder brother's daughter in marriage.

items.text: Teach your son that labor breeds virtue and idleness breeds vice.
items.quote: 夫民勞則思，思則善心生；逸則淫，淫則忘善 — When people labor they think, and thinking produces good; when idle they become dissolute, and dissoluteness forgets good.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 序 … 小學 內篇 立教 4

items.text: Train the child in good habits from infancy: teach them to eat with the right hand, speak and respond properly, and respect their elders.
items.quote: 子能食食，敎以右手。能言男唯女兪。稍有知則敎之以恭敬尊長。

items.text: Choose a teacher for the child from among the household's mothers or other suitable women: one who is generous, kind, gentle, respectful, careful, and sparing of words.
items.quote: 必求其寬裕、慈惠、溫良、恭敬，愼而寡言者

items.text: Choose a wet nurse for the newborn from a good family, one who is gentle and careful, for a bad wet nurse ruins the child's character.
items.quote: 求乳母必擇良家婦人稍溫謹者

items.text: Never deceive the young child; always show them what is right and true, so that they learn uprightness.
items.quote: 幼子常視毋誑

items.text: As the child grows, teach them to yield to elders, to feel shame at wrong, and to learn numbers and the directions.
items.quote: 必後長者。始敎之讓。示以廉恥。

items.text: At age ten, send the boy to an outside teacher; he should live away from home and begin formal study of the classics.
items.quote: 十年出就外傅，居宿於外

items.text: Keep the daughter at home after age ten; have her instructed in gentleness, obedience, and all the skills of a woman's work.
items.quote: 女子十年不出。姆敎婉娩聽從。

items.text: Love and obey your parents; from youth, learn to serve them with proper manners and filial devotion.
items.quote: 愛親，敬長

items.text: Show respect to all elders: when going out or at meals, follow after them; yield to them in all things.
items.quote: 必後長者

items.text: Do not strike or revile older brothers and sisters; treat them with respect and deference.
items.quote: 敺擊兄姊

items.text: When the child shows disrespect or violence toward elders, rebuke and correct him immediately; do not laugh or encourage it, lest the habit harden.
items.quote: 有不識尊卑長幼者，則嚴訶禁之。

items.text: Guard the child's reading: forbid books that are not of the sages, lest they confuse and mislead his mind.
items.quote: 其異端非聖賢之書，傅宜禁之。勿使妄觀，以惑亂其志。
items.conflict: Excludes the Bible and Christian literature, which a Christian would deem essential.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 外篇 嘉言 48 … 小學 外篇 嘉言 77

items.text: Heed your father-in-law's warning: do not by rivalry or favoritism divide brothers.
items.quote: 皆汝婦人所作...若等寧有是耶 — All this is done by you women... Do you dare be like that?

items.text: Love your brothers as you love your parents; do not treat them as strangers or enemies.
items.quote: 獨愛父母之子，卻輕於己之子。甚者至若仇敵 — He loves his parents' children less than his own, even as enemies.

items.text: Do not cease to be kind to your brothers even when they do not return it; do not imitate their faults.
items.quote: 兄弟宣相好，不要相學...己施之而已 — Brothers should love each other, not imitate each other; just keep giving without expecting return.

items.text: Help the poor among your clansmen without regard to closeness, since all are equally the seed of your ancestors.
items.quote: 苟祖宗之意無親疎，則飢寒者，吾安得不恤也 — If the ancestors' will makes no distinction, how can I not pity the cold and hungry?

items.text: Govern your house by rites and law; assign each his office; measure income against outlay; provide for all according to rank, and keep a surplus for emergencies.
items.quote: 凡爲家長必謹守禮法，以御羣子弟及家眾...制財用之節，量入以爲出...常須稍存贏餘 — Every head of a family must strictly keep rites and law to govern the children and household; regulate expenses, measure income against outlay, always keep a surplus.

items.text: Care for your parents in their old age, even retiring from public life to serve them.
items.quote: 孝友先生朱仁軌隱居養親 — Master Zhu Rengui, being filial and fraternal, lived in seclusion to care for his parents.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 外篇 嘉言 23 … 小學 外篇 嘉言 47

items.text: During mourning for father or mother, before the Great Xiang sacrifice, do not eat meat or drink wine.
items.quote: 凡居父母之喪者，大祥之前皆未可食肉飮酒。 — During mourning for parents, before the Great Xiang, do not eat meat or drink wine.

items.text: While mourning, live in a bare hut outside the middle gate; for a father wear unhemmed sackcloth, sleep on straw, and do not socialize.
items.quote: 父母之喪，中門之外擇樸陋之室爲丈夫喪次。 — During mourning for parents, choose a bare hut outside the middle gate for the men.

items.text: Do not give offerings to monks or perform Buddhist rites for the dead; it is false and cannot help them.
items.quote: 凡有喪事無不供佛飯僧。 — At funerals they all offer to Buddha and feed monks.

items.text: Never speak of shamans or talismans; do nothing superstitious.
items.quote: 吾家巫覡?符章，絶於言議，汝曹所見。 勿爲妖妄。 — In our family, shamans and talismans are never spoken of; do not be deluded.

items.text: On your birthday, when parents are gone, be doubly sorrowful; do not set out wine and music.
items.quote: 人無父母，生日當倍悲痛。 更安忍置酒張樂，以爲樂。 — When one has no parents, on his birthday he should be doubly grieved; how can he bear to set out wine and music?

items.text: Keep one wife; do not multiply concubines, for that teaches disorder.
items.quote: 一夫一婦庶人之職也。 — One husband one wife is the duty of commoners.

items.text: In arranging marriage, first examine the character and family ways of the prospective spouse; do not covet wealth or rank.
items.quote: 凡議婚姻，當先察其壻與婦之性行及家法何如。 勿苟慕其富貴。 — In discussing marriage, first look at the character and family discipline of the groom and bride; do not carelessly admire wealth and rank.

items.text: Marry your daughter into a family better than yours, and take a daughter-in-law from a family not better than yours.
items.quote: 嫁女必須勝吾家者。... 娶婦必須不若吾家者。 — For marrying a daughter, must choose a family better than ours; for taking a wife, must choose not better than ours.

items.text: Do not remarry; starvation is a small matter, loss of chastity is great.
items.quote: 餓死事極小，失節事極大。 — Death by starvation is very small; loss of chastity is very great.
items.conflict: Scripture permits widows to remarry (1 Cor 7:8-9).

items.text: In the home, do not meddle in external affairs; use your intelligence to support your husband and counsel his shortcomings.
items.quote: 婦主中饋，唯事酒食衣服之禮耳。... 如有聦明才智，識達古今，正當輔佐君子，勸其不足。 — A wife presides over food and clothing; if she has intelligence, she should support her husband and counsel his deficiencies.

items.text: Love your brother; you are one body divided; do not let outsiders weaken your fraternal affection.
items.quote: 兄弟者分形連氣之人也。 — Brothers are one body divided.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 內篇 稽古 6 … 小學 內篇 稽古 22

items.text: Serve your parents with all your strength and fulfill a child's duty; do not resent them but reproach yourself.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 稽古 6-22
items.quote: 竭力耕田共爲子職 — Work the fields with all your might, doing a son's duty.

items.text: Serve your parents knowing you always fall short; cherish each day with them, for time is short.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 稽古 6-22
items.quote: 孝子愛日 — A filial child treasures the days.

items.text: Attend your father morning, noon, and night; ask after his comfort, and if he is unwell, oversee his meals and do not rest until he recovers.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 稽古 6-22
items.quote: 朝於王季日三 — Three times a day he visited his father.

items.text: When your father is ill, tend him without rest, and match your own meals to his to gauge his strength.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 稽古 6-22
items.quote: 文王一飯亦一飯 — If Wen ate one bowl, Wu ate one bowl.

items.text: Serve the dead as if they were living; carry forward your parents' will and complete their work.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 稽古 6-22
items.quote: 事死如事生，事亡如事存 — Serve the dead as living; serve the departed as present.
items.conflict: Contrary to Scripture: worship belongs to God alone; the dead cannot be served (Deut 18:11).

items.text: Serve your father with utter deference; do not act on your own initiative, but hold his commands as a precious burden.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 稽古 6-22
items.quote: 行無專制，事無由己 — He acted with no self-will, did nothing of his own accord.

items.text: When caring for your parents, nourish not just their body but their heart; honor their wishes even in small things.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 稽古 6-22
items.quote: 若曾子則可謂養志也 — Zengzi may be said to have nourished his parents' will.

items.text: Keep your body whole and your conduct honorable, for it is your parents' gift; in every step and word, remember them.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 稽古 6-22
items.quote: 父母全而生之。子全而歸之 — Parents give a whole body; a son returns it whole.

items.text: When your parents are angry and punish you, accept it humbly; do not show resentment, but make them pity you.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 稽古 6-22
items.quote: 父母怒之，不作於意，不見於色 — When parents are angry, not to harbor resentment or show it.

items.text: Mourn your parents with deep grief for the full three years, not slackening early.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 稽古 6-22
items.quote: 三年憂 — three years of grief.
items.conflict: No prescribed mourning period in Scripture; grief is not meritorious.

items.text: If your father errs, remonstrate with him up to three times; if he will not listen, still follow him with tears.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 稽古 6-22
items.quote: 父有過，子三諫不聽，則隨而號之 — If a father errs, a son remonstrates three times; if not heard, follow weeping.

items.text: Even in old age, delight your parents with playful, childlike acts to make them happy.
items.citation: 小學, 內篇 稽古 6-22
items.quote: 行年七十作嬰兒戲 — At seventy he played children's games.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 內篇 敬身 15 … 小學 內篇 敬身 37

items.text: When you meet one you respect, be quick and attentive, not slow or casual.
items.quote: 見所尊者齊遬 — When seeing one whom he respects, he is quick and respectful.

items.text: In your village, defer to your elders: be humble and not forward, as if unable to speak.
items.quote: 孔子於郷黨恂恂如也。似不能言者。 郷黨尙齒故也。 — Confucius in his village was humble, as if unable to speak; because the village honors age.

items.text: Be filial to your father and mother.
items.quote: 與幼者言言孝弟於父兄 — When speaking with the young, talk of filial piety and fraternal duty to father and elder brother.

items.text: Be brotherly to your elder brother.
items.quote: 與幼者言言孝弟於父兄 — When speaking with the young, talk of filial piety and fraternal duty to father and elder brother.

items.text: When handing something to an elder, do not kneel if he stands or stand if he sits, so as not to make him bend or stretch.
items.quote: 授立不跪，授坐不立。 爲煩尊者俛仰受之。 — When handing to one standing, do not kneel; when handing to one sitting, do not stand—to avoid troubling the superior to bend or look up.

items.text: At your coming-of-age, abandon childish aims and cultivate mature virtue; be respectful and careful in your bearing.
items.quote: 棄爾幼志，順爾成德 — Abandon your childish aims; follow your mature virtue.

items.text: While your parents are alive, do not trim your cap or clothes in plain white, lest you resemble a mourner.
items.quote: 父母存冠衣不純素。 爲其有喪像也。 — While his parents are alive, a son does not use plain white for the borders of cap or clothes, because that would resemble mourning.

items.text: While mourning a parent, do not wear jade or other ornaments until the mourning is complete.
items.quote: 去喪，無所不佩。 — After the mourning is ended, he wears all his ornaments again.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 內篇 明倫 1 … 小學 內篇 明倫 11

items.text: At cockcrow go to them, speak gently, ask after cold, pain, and itching, and soothe them; keep them warm in winter and cool in summer, and settle them at night.
items.quote: 下氣，怡聲，問衣燠寒?疾痛?苛癢 — gently, pleasantly, ask about cold, pain, itching.

items.text: When they go out or come in, walk before or behind and respectfully support them; ask what they desire and bring it with a gentle face, and let them taste it before you retire.
items.quote: 出入則或先或後，而敬扶持之...問所欲而敬進之，柔色以溫之 — when going out or coming in, support them; ask what they want and bring it gently.

items.text: Take charge of cooking and meals, ensure they are clean, and prepare the morning food.
items.quote: 凡烹調飮膳婦人之職也...務令淸潔 — all cooking and meals are the woman's duty; make sure they are clean.

items.text: Rise at first light, wash, dress, tidy the beds, sweep the rooms, hall, and courtyard, arrange the mats, and attend to your own tasks.
items.quote: 雞初鳴咸盥，漱，衣服，歛枕?簟，灑掃室?堂及庭，布席，各從其事 — at cockcrow wash, dress, tidy beds, sweep, arrange mats, each do their task.

items.text: When they are about to sit or recline, bring the mat and ask which direction they prefer, and arrange their bedding accordingly.
items.quote: 父母舅姑將坐，奉席請何郷。將衽，長者奉席請何趾 — when parents sit, bring mat and ask direction; when they recline, ask which way their feet point.

items.text: Do not move their clothes, bedding, mats, pillow, or stool; revere their staff and shoes and do not go near them; use their cups and vessels only for eating leftovers, and do not eat or drink their regular food except what they leave over.
items.quote: 父母舅姑之衣衾?簟席?枕幾不傳。杖?屨祗敬之勿敢近...非餕莫敢用 — their clothes, mats, pillow, stool not moved; staff, shoes revered; utensils only for leftovers.

items.text: In their presence answer respectfully and move carefully; avoid yawning, stretching, spitting, and exposing undergarments; clean away their spittle, and wash or mend their soiled or torn clothes.
items.quote: 應唯敬對...不敢噦?噫?嚏?咳?欠?伸...褻衣衾不見裏...衣裳垢和灰請澣，衣裳綻裂紉箴請補綴 — answer respectfully; no yawning, stretching; undergarments not shown; wash or mend clothes.

items.text: Serve them with deep love, showing a gentle expression and careful manner as if holding jade or a full vessel; do not be stern, dignified, or formal.
items.quote: 孝子之有深愛者必有和氣...嚴威儼恪非所以事親也 — deep love brings gentle face; sternness is not the way to serve parents.

items.text: Do not occupy the place of honor, sit in the middle, walk in the middle of the path, stand in the middle of the door, or use the east steps; do not presume to act for your father, do not set limits for feasts, do not serve as the personator in sacrifice, and do not criticize or laugh carelessly.
items.quote: 居不主奧，坐不中席，行不中道，立不中門...祭祀不為屍...不苟訾，不苟笑 — do not occupy the honored corner, center seat, middle path or door; not be the personator; no careless criticism or laughter.

items.text: While parents are alive, do not travel far; if you must travel, have a fixed destination so they know where you are.
items.quote: 父母在不遠遊，遊必有方 — while parents live, do not travel far; if travel, have a direction.

items.text: While parents are alive, do not promise a friend that you will die for him, for your life belongs to your parents.
items.quote: 父母存，不許友以死 — while parents live, do not promise a friend to die for him.

items.text: Obey their commands without opposition or laziness; accept what they give, even if you dislike it, taste or wear it, and wait for their word before putting it away.
items.quote: 父母舅姑之命，勿逆，勿怠...雖不耆必嘗而待，雖不欲必服而待 — do not disobey or neglect parents' commands; even if you dislike food, taste it; if clothes, wear them.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 內篇 稽古 45 … 小學 外篇 嘉言 9

items.text: Teach your children what is right and do not let them learn evil.
items.quote: 愛子敎之以義方，弗納於邪 — If you love your son, teach him the right way; do not let him fall into evil.

items.text: Be filial to your parents.
items.quote: 子孝 — a son is filial.

items.text: Love your younger siblings.
items.quote: 兄愛 — an elder brother loves.

items.text: Respect your elder siblings.
items.quote: 弟敬 — a younger brother respects.

items.text: First teach children to be composed, respectful, and diligent in serving; do not let them become proud and lazy.
items.quote: 敎小兒，先要安詳恭敬。 — In teaching young children, first require composure and respect.

items.text: Educate children first in filial piety, brotherly respect, loyalty, trustworthiness, propriety, justice, and shame; use stories of such deeds.
items.quote: 必先以孝悌、忠信、禮義、廉恥等事 — must first use matters of filial piety, brotherly respect, loyalty, trustworthiness, propriety, justice, and shame.

items.text: Do not let your children waste their ambition on idle hobbies; teach them the classics and restraint.
items.quote: 子弟凡百玩好，皆奪志。 — All kinds of hobbies for young people steal their will.

items.text: Teach children through songs that include sweeping, answering, and serving elders, so they learn willingly.
items.quote: 略言敎童子，灑掃、應對、事長之節，令朝夕歌之。 — briefly speak of teaching children the duties of sweeping, answering, and serving elders, and have them sing these daily.

items.text: When you hear of others' faults, treat it like hearing your parents' names: you may hear but never speak of it.
items.quote: 聞人過失，如聞父母之名。耳可得聞，口不可得言也。 — Hearing others' faults is like hearing your parents' names: your ears may hear, but your mouth must not speak.

items.text: Do not do evil because it is small; do not neglect good because it is small.
items.quote: 勿以惡小而爲之，勿以善小而不爲。 — Do not do evil because it is small; do not omit good because it is small.

items.text: Cultivate your character through tranquility and frugality; study requires quietness, and without learning you cannot broaden your talents.
items.quote: 靜以脩身，儉以養德。非澹泊，無以明志。非寧靜，無以致遠。 — Cultivate yourself through tranquility, nourish virtue through frugality; without indifference to fame you cannot make your will clear; without quietness you cannot reach far.

items.text: Avoid the five vices that bring shame to your ancestors and ruin your family; remember your ancestors' faithfulness and hard work.
items.quote: 夫壞名災己，辱先喪家。其失尤大者五。 — To ruin your name, harm yourself, disgrace your ancestors, and destroy your family: there are five especially great faults.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 外篇 嘉言 10 … 小學 外篇 嘉言 22

items.text: Admonish and teach him to pursue virtue, filial piety, humility, and diligent study; guard against arrogance, dissipation, drinking, and loose talk.
items.quote: 戒，爾學立身，莫若先孝悌 — Warn: first learn filial piety and brotherly respect.

items.text: Teach them to be good: avoid improper sights, sounds, words, and places; associate only with the virtuous and shun the wicked.
items.quote: 吉也者，目不觀非禮之色，耳不聽非禮之聲 — The good person does not look at what is not propriety, nor listen to what is not propriety.

items.text: Instruct him to set his mind on the Way, be loyal and faithful, conduct himself with dignity and prudence, handle affairs with discernment, and above all govern his heart and body, paying close attention to food and sex.
items.quote: 立志以明道?希文自期待，立心以忠信?不欺爲主本 — Set your resolve to clarify the Way; ground your heart in loyalty and faithfulness.

items.text: Nurture her children with kindness.
items.quote: 母慈，能養其下 — The mother is kind and able to nurture those below her.

items.text: Love his younger brother.
items.quote: 兄友，能愛其弟 — The elder brother is friendly, able to love his younger brother.

items.text: Respect his elder brother.
items.quote: 弟恭，能敬其兄 — The younger brother is respectful, able to respect his elder brother.

items.text: Do not abandon or fail to support her; hold fast together even in poverty.
items.quote: 夫婦有恩，貧窮相守爲恩 — Husband and wife have mutual kindness; in poverty they keep together as kindness.

items.text: Do not remarry after your husband's death; remain faithful to his memory.
items.quote: 夫喪改嫁，皆是無恩也 — If the wife remarries after the husband's death, that is lack of kindness.
items.conflict: Scripture allows a widow to remarry (1 Cor 7:39).

items.text: In all matters, great or small, do not act on your own; first consult the head of the household.
items.quote: 凡諸卑幼，事無大小，毋得專行。必諮稟於家長 — All juniors, in matters great or small, must not act on their own; they must ask the household head.

items.text: Receive your parents' commands, write them down, carry them out promptly, and report back; if you cannot do it, explain respectfully, and follow if not harmful.
items.quote: 凡子受父母之命，必籍記而佩之，時省而速行之，事畢則返命焉 — Whenever a son receives his parents' command, he must write it down, keep it, carry it out quickly, and report back when done.

items.text: When your parent is ill, do not leave them to a poor doctor; learn enough medicine to care for them properly.
items.quote: 病臥於床，委之庸醫，比之不慈不孝。事親者，亦不可不知醫 — To leave a sick parent to a quack is unfilial; one serving parents must know medicine.

items.text: Maintain the family temple and offer the seasonal sacrifices; do not neglect the rites for the dead, but give them more honor than the living.
items.quote: 家必有廟。凡事死之禮，當厚於奉生者 — Every family must have a temple; rites for the dead should be richer than serving the living.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the command to worship God alone (Exod 20:3-5).

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 外篇 善行 44 … 小學 外篇 善行 58

items.text: Make your children work diligently in the old fields to supply their own food and clothing; do not add surplus wealth that breeds idleness.
items.citation: 小學, 外篇 善行 44
items.quote: 令子孫勤力其中，足以共衣食 — Make your sons and grandsons work diligently, enough to supply their own food and clothing.

items.text: Leave your descendants peace, not peril.
items.citation: 小學, 外篇 善行 45
items.quote: 世人皆遺之以危。今獨遺之以安 — The world bequeaths them danger; I alone bequeath them peace.

items.text: Obey your elder brother in all daily matters; do not act without his command.
items.citation: 小學, 外篇 善行 47
items.quote: 坐食進退，孝芬不命則不敢也 — In sitting, eating, advancing or retiring, they did not dare without Xiaofen's command.

items.text: Serve your uncle's widow as you would your own mother, consulting her on all family matters.
items.citation: 小學, 外篇 善行 47
items.quote: 承奉叔母李氏，若事所生 — Served their uncle's wife Lady Li as if serving their own mother.

items.text: Love one another and share everything, whether in plenty or in want.
items.citation: 小學, 外篇 善行 47
items.quote: 諸婦亦相親愛，有無共之 — The wives also loved one another and shared what they had and had not.

items.text: Govern your household with diligence, frugality, respect, and forbearance; regulate it with the rites of capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice.
items.citation: 小學, 外篇 善行 48
items.quote: 禦家以四敎。勤?儉?恭?恕。正家以四禮。冠?昏?喪?祭。 — Govern the family with four teachings: diligence, frugality, respect, forbearance; regulate it with four rites: capping, marriage, mourning, sacrifice.

items.text: Bear with one another patiently; if you do, the family will be harmonious.
items.citation: 小學, 外篇 善行 49
items.quote: 苟能相與忍之，則家道雍睦矣 — If you can bear with one another, the family will be harmonious.

items.text: Prepare delicious food for your parents and ask after their health every day.
items.citation: 小學, 外篇 善行 50
items.quote: 入廚具甘旨，上堂問起居 — Go into the kitchen to prepare delicious food, go to the hall to ask after their health.

items.text: Serve your uncle with the same respect as you served your father.
items.citation: 小學, 外篇 善行 51
items.quote: 事公權如事公綽 — Served Gongquan as he had served Gongchuo.

items.text: Arrange marriages for orphaned or widowed female relatives without delay, even if the dowry is modest.
items.citation: 小學, 外篇 善行 51
items.quote: 姑姊妹姪有孤嫠者，雖疎遠必爲擇壻嫁之 — For aunts, sisters, and nieces who were orphans or widows, even if distant, he would choose husbands and marry them off.

items.text: Do not lose your temper with your wife even when provoked; keep a calm and kind demeanor.
items.citation: 小學, 外篇 善行 55
items.quote: 神色不異。乃徐言曰，羹爛汝手乎 — His expression unchanged, he slowly said, 'Did the soup burn your hand?'

items.text: Give your mother the best food, even if you and your guest eat plainly.
items.citation: 小學, 外篇 善行 58
items.quote: 供其母，自以草蔬與客同飯 — He served his mother, and himself ate vegetables with the guest.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 內篇 敬身 38 … 小學 內篇 稽古 5

items.text: While pregnant, guard your eyes, ears, and mouth from evil; after birth, teach your child so that he may become wise and virtuous.
items.quote: 目不視惡色，耳不聽淫聲，口不出敖言 — Do not look at evil sights, listen to lewd sounds, or speak arrogant words.

items.text: Choose a good environment for your child's upbringing, such as moving near a place of learning, so that your child may grow up in wholesome surroundings.
items.quote: 此眞可以居子矣 — This is truly a place where a child can live.

items.text: Do not deceive your child; if you promise something, fulfill it, lest you teach him to be untrustworthy.
items.quote: 是敎之不信 — This is teaching him dishonesty.

items.text: Teach your son the Book of Songs so he may learn to speak, and the Book of Rites so he may learn to stand.
items.quote: 不學詩無以言...不學禮無以立 — If he does not learn the Odes, he has nothing to speak; if he does not learn the Rites, he has nothing to stand.

items.text: Teach your son the Odes of Zhounan and Shaonan, for without them a man is as one standing with his face to a wall, unable to see or move.
items.quote: 人而不爲周南?召南，其猶正牆面而立也與 — A man who does not study the Zhounan and Shaonan is like one standing with his face to a wall.

items.text: Even if your parents are stubborn or harsh, maintain harmony through filial piety and do not allow them to fall into evil.
items.quote: 克諧以孝，烝烝。 乂不格姦 — He harmonized with them through filial piety, and they did not become evil.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 外篇 善行 1 … 小學 外篇 善行 13

items.text: Train your children with strict rules in even the smallest matters, such as what they may eat.
items.quote: 至微細事，敎之必有法度。如飮食之類，飯羹許更益，魚肉不更進也。

items.text: Obey your parents' rules about dress, sitting, and places you may go; do not sit or remove proper clothing without their word.
items.quote: 終日不命之坐不敢坐也。日必冠帶以見長者。

items.text: Do not stay away from your parents; return and care for them, and let no long time pass without attending them.
items.quote: 諸生有久不省親者乎？明日謁城還養者二十軰，有三年不歸侍者，斥之。

items.text: Carry your mother on your back through danger and work as a laborer to supply her with all she needs.
items.quote: 革負母逃難，備經險阻，常採拾以爲養。裸跣行傭，以供母。

items.text: Even if your father drives you out, keep serving him; sweep and attend him daily until he relents.
items.quote: 包日夜號泣不能去。至被敺杖，不得已廬於舍外，旦入而灑掃。晨昏不廢。

items.text: When dividing the family property, take the inferior portion and help your siblings when they are in need.
items.quote: 奴婢引其老者曰，與我共事久，若不能使也。田廬取其荒頓者曰，吾少時所理，意所戀也。器物取其朽敗者曰，我素所服食，身口所安也。弟子數破其產輒復賑給。

items.text: When your parents are ill, do not loosen your clothes and taste their medicine yourself.
items.quote: 父母有疾，衣不解帶，湯藥必親嘗。

items.text: Serve your stepmother respectfully and seek to fulfill her desires even in hardship.
items.quote: 母嘗欲生魚。時天寒冰凍。祥解衣將剖冰求之。冰忽自解，雙鯉躍出。

items.text: Live by your father's grave and bow to it daily in mourning; do not serve those who killed him.
items.quote: 廬於墓側，旦夕常至墓所拜跪，攀栢悲號。及司馬氏簒魏，裒終身未嘗西向而坐。
items.conflict: Do not bow to graves or speak to the dead; honor your father by obeying God, not by rites to the departed.

items.text: Serve your parents with a cheerful face; in summer cool their bed, in winter warm it with your body, and give them the best food even if you lack clothing.
items.quote: 事親色養。夏則扇枕席，冬則以身溫被。隆冬盛寒，體常無全衣，而親極滋味。

items.text: Attend to your wife with due care and treat her as your own.
items.quote: 居家則事父兄，敎子弟，侍妻妾。

items.text: Serve your elder brother as you serve your father.
items.quote: 事父兄

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 外篇 善行 59 … 小學 外篇 善行 81

items.text: When visiting your father at his official post, alight before the gate, treat his subordinates with formal courtesy, and avoid easy familiarity.
items.quote: 常於戟門外下馬。呼幕賓爲丈，皆許納拜。未嘗笑語欵洽。 — He would always dismount outside the gate with spears; he called the aides 'sir' and allowed them to bow; he never engaged in light talk or close familiarity.

items.text: When your father refuses an extravagance, do not press for it; accept his judgment.
items.quote: 女子不復敢言 — The girl did not dare to speak again.

items.text: Warn your children that costly luxuries are evil things that bring ruin.
items.quote: 但一釵七十萬，此妖物也。必與禍相隨。 — But a hairpin costing seventy thousand is an evil thing; it will surely bring disaster.

items.text: Restrain your wife from costly adornment; keep your household in order.
items.quote: 馮以卑位貪寶貨，已不能正其家 — Feng, in a low position, coveted precious goods, and so could not keep his household in order.

items.text: Serve your mother with utmost filial devotion.
items.quote: 事母至孝 — He served his mother with utmost filial piety.

items.text: Keep your household's dress simple and clean; let no silk or brocade enter the house, and clothe women in plain hues.
items.quote: 綺羅錦繡不入於室。曰，君子非黃白不禦。婦人則有靑碧。 — Silk and brocade do not enter his house. He said, 'A gentleman does not wear yellow or white; women wear blue-green.'

items.text: Keep your household accustomed to thrift; do not let them grow accustomed to luxury.
items.quote: 家人習奢已久，不能頓儉，必至失所 — If the family has long been accustomed to extravagance, they cannot suddenly become frugal, and will surely lose their place.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 內篇 明倫 59 … 小學 內篇 明倫 76

items.text: Do not remarry; once joined to your husband, remain faithful to him all your life.
items.quote: 壹與之齊，終身不改。故夫死不嫁。 — Once united with him, she does not change for life; therefore when her husband dies she does not remarry.
items.conflict: A widow is free to remarry, only in the Lord (1 Cor 7:39); the Bible does not command perpetual celibacy.

items.text: At his wedding, give him the cup and charge him to go and receive his wife, to carry on the ancestral temple services, and to lead her with reverence and constancy.
items.quote: 父醮子，命之曰，往迎爾相，承我宗事，勗帥以敬，先姒之嗣。若則有常。 — The father gives the cup to his son and commands: Go and receive your helper, continue our ancestral temple affairs, strive to lead her with respect, she will succeed our former ancestress; your conduct must be constant.

items.text: Continue the ancestral temple rites and do not let them fail.
items.quote: 承我宗事 — Continue our ancestral temple affairs.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with the first commandment; honor parents but worship God alone.

items.text: When sending her off in marriage, charge her to be reverent and careful, and morning and night never to disobey the commands of her parents-in-law.
items.quote: 父送女，命之曰，戒之敬之夙夜無違命。 — The father sends off his daughter and commands: Be cautious and respectful; morning and night do not disobey the commands of your parents-in-law.

items.text: When giving her the sash and handkerchief, charge her to be diligent and reverent, and morning and night never to neglect her household duties.
items.quote: 母施衿結帨曰，勉之敬之夙夜無違宮事。 — The mother ties the sash and handkerchief and says: Be diligent and respectful; morning and night do not neglect household duties.

items.text: Be trustworthy and faithful in serving your husband, for trustworthiness is the virtue of a wife.
items.quote: 信事人也。信婦德也。 — Trustworthiness is what serves others; it is the virtue of a wife.

items.text: While at home, obey your father and do not act on your own initiative.
items.quote: 在家從父 — While at home, follow your father.

items.text: After marriage, obey your husband and do not take independent authority.
items.quote: 適人從夫 — After marriage, follow your husband.

items.text: After your husband's death, obey your son and do not act on your own.
items.quote: 夫死從子 — After your husband's death, follow your son.
items.conflict: A mother is not subject to her son's authority; she is to be honored and provided for, not ruled (1 Tim 5:4).

items.text: Love your parents from childhood, as all children naturally do.
items.quote: 孩提之童無不知愛其親。 — Even young children know to love their parents.

items.text: Respect your elder brother; when grown, show him the honor due to an elder sibling.
items.quote: 及其長也，無不知敬其兄也。 — When they grow up, they all know to respect their elder brothers.

items.text: Keep proper separation between you: do not share the same clothes rack, do not bathe together, and do not enter each other's inner or outer quarters.
items.quote: 男女不同椸枷，不敢共湢浴。男不入女不出。 — Men and women do not share the same clothes rack, do not bathe together; men do not enter the inner quarters, women do not go out.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 外篇 善行 14 … 小學 外篇 善行 28

items.text: Serve your mother-in-law with devoted care, even to nourishing her with your own milk when she cannot eat grain.
items.quote: 升堂乳其姑 — went into the hall and suckled her mother-in-law.

items.text: When a parent is ill, set aside all other duties, return home, and attend with such devotion that you would even take the illness upon yourself.
items.quote: 每夕稽顙北辰，求以身代 — every evening he bowed his head to the North Star and begged to take his father's place.
items.conflict: Praying to a star (North Dipper) is idolatry; we must pray only to God.

items.text: Mourn your parent with true grief; do not end mourning or delay burial even in poverty, and deny yourself comforts until the rites are complete.
items.quote: 母喪去官，哀毀踰禮... 八年不得營葬 — went into mourning for his mother and left office, grieving beyond the rites... for eight years could not arrange burial.

items.text: Seek out your separated mother, give up your own position if needed, and care for her in old age.
items.quote: 棄官入秦，與家人訣。誓不見母不復還 — gave up his office, went to Qin, and took leave of his family, swearing not to return until he saw his mother.

items.text: Care for your younger siblings and their orphaned children, providing for their marriages and burials as you are able.
items.quote: 拊其弟妹益篤，爲買田宅居之... 嫁兄弟之孤女二人 — cared for his younger brother and sisters even more, bought them land and houses... arranged marriages for two orphaned daughters of his brothers.

items.text: When a death occurs, do not summon Buddhist monks or use their rites; bury the dead according to the family's proper rites.
items.quote: 治喪不用浮屠 — in conducting funerals he did not use Buddhist rites.

items.text: Do not allow your child to falsify his origin for advantage; teach him that serving a ruler begins with honesty.
items.quote: 汝虔州人而貫開封戸籍。欲求事君而先欺君，可乎 — You are a man of Qianzhou, but you would claim Kaifeng registration. You wish to serve the ruler, yet you begin by deceiving him—is that right?

items.text: When your child brings you gifts from office, do not just rejoice; ask whether the money was honestly earned.
items.quote: 見親表中，仕宦者將錢物上其父母。父母但知喜悅，竟不問此物從何而來 — when officials give money to their parents, the parents only rejoice and never ask where it came from.

items.text: Keep the promise you made to your husband; if he dies, fulfill his charge to care for his mother.
items.quote: 夫去時，屬妾以供養老母。妾旣許諾之 — When my husband left, he charged me to support his old mother, and I promised.

items.text: Do not remarry, even if your parents urge it, if you have vowed to your dead husband to care for his mother; remain chaste to keep your word.
items.quote: 其父母哀其少無子而早寡也，將取嫁之。孝婦...欲自殺 — her parents, pitying her youth, childlessness and early widowhood, wished to marry her off; the filial wife... threatened to kill herself.
items.conflict: 1 Cor 7:39 permits a widow to remarry; a vow beyond Scripture is not binding.

items.text: Follow your husband's lead, lay aside luxury, and share his toil and poverty.
items.quote: 妻乃悉歸侍御服飾，更著短布裳，與宣共挽鹿車歸郷裡拜姑 — she returned all her fine clothes and adornments, put on a short cloth skirt, and together with Huan pulled the deer cart back to his village to bow to his mother.

items.text: Continue to offer the ancestral sacrifices for your husband's line as long as you live.
items.quote: 終奉祭祀 — she continued to perform the sacrifices to the end.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 外篇 善行 29 … 小學 外篇 善行 43

items.text: Remain faithful to your deceased husband and do not remarry, even if your family tries to force you; preserve your integrity through all changes.
items.quote: 聞仁者不以盛衰改節，義者不以存亡易心。 — The benevolent do not change integrity with prosperity or decline; the righteous do not change heart with survival or death.
items.conflict: Scripture permits a widow to remarry (1 Cor 7:39); self-mutilation is not required.

items.text: Protect your mother-in-law even at the risk of your own life; do not abandon her in danger, for human duty is above beast.
items.quote: 況在於姑而可委棄乎。若萬一危禍，豈宜獨生。 — How can I abandon my mother-in-law? If danger comes, how could I live alone?

items.text: Take responsibility to keep the household united; when brothers or their wives seek division, first reprove yourself and correct your own conduct.
items.quote: 繆肜汝脩身，謹行，學聖人之法，將以齊整風俗。柰何不能正其家乎。 — Miao Tong, you cultivate yourself and practice carefully, studying the sages' way to order customs; why can you not set your own house in order?

items.text: Esteem your brothers above land; give up property rather than break brotherly love.
items.quote: 天下難得者兄弟，易求者田地。假令得田地，失兄弟心如何。 — Brothers are hard to come by; land is easy to get. If you gain land but lose your brother's heart, what good is it?

items.text: Protect your elder brother from unjust punishment; plead with your mother to stop her cruelty, and share his burdens.
items.quote: 見祥被楚撻，輒涕泣抱持。... 覽與祥倶。 — When he saw Xiang being beaten, he would weep and embrace him; ... Lan shared Xiang's labors.

items.text: Preserve your deceased brother's only son even if it costs your own child; his line must not be cut off.
items.quote: 吾弟蚤亡唯有一息。理不可絶。止應自棄我兒耳。 — My brother died early leaving one son; his line must not be cut off, so we should abandon our own child.
items.conflict: Parents must provide for their own children (1 Tim 5:8); cannot abandon one child for another.

items.text: Do not abandon a sick brother even in a plague; tend him day and night at the risk of your life.
items.quote: 袞性不畏病。遂親自扶持晝夜不眠。 — Gun said, 'I am not afraid of disease,' and personally tended him day and night without sleep.

items.text: Revere your elder brother as a father; do not sit or eat before him, serve him first, and send him the firstfruits of every season.
items.quote: 昆季相事有如父子。... 椿不命坐，津不敢坐。... 食則津親授匙箸，味皆先嘗。椿命食然後食。 — The brothers served each other like father and son; if Chun did not tell Jin to sit, Jin did not dare sit; at meals Jin handed him spoon and chopsticks, tasted first, and ate only after Chun said eat.

items.text: Do not reproach a younger brother for a loss he caused in drunkenness; bear it patiently and keep your composure.
items.quote: 弘聞無所恠問，直答曰，作脯。... 顏色自若讀書不輟。 — Hong asked no question, only said, 'Make dried meat,' and continued reading undisturbed.

items.text: Serve your aged brother as a strict father and protect him as an infant; ask if he is hungry or cold.
items.quote: 伯康年將八十，公奉之如嚴父，保之如嬰兒。每食少頃則問曰，得無餓乎。天少冷則拊其背曰，衣得無薄乎。 — Bokang was nearly eighty; Gong served him like a strict father, protected him like an infant; after each meal he asked, 'Are you hungry?' when it was cold he patted his back and said, 'Are your clothes too thin?'

items.text: Personally tend your father's most private needs; wash his soiled garments and toilet utensils without letting him know, and do it as a constant service.
items.quote: 每五日洗沐歸謁親，入子舎，竊問侍者，取親中帬厠牏身自浣灑，復與侍者，不敢令萬石君知之，以爲常。 — Every five days he returned to see his parent, went to his father's room, secretly asked the servants, took his father's undergarments and toilet vessel, washed them himself, gave them back, and did not let his father know; this was his constant practice.

items.text: Do not scold your adult son's faults with angry words; instead show your displeasure by not eating until he repents and the family intercedes for him.
items.quote: 子孫有過失不誚讓。爲便坐，對案不食。然後諸子相責，因長老肉祖固謝罪，改之乃許。 — When descendants had faults, he did not scold; he sat apart, faced the table and did not eat; then the sons reproved each other, and through elders they begged forgiveness, and only after reforms did he allow it.

heading: 小學 Xiaoxue · Elementary Learning (Zhu Xi) · 小學 內篇 明倫 12 … 小學 內篇 明倫 33

items.text: Have no private goods or savings; bring all your income from salary and land to your parents and parents-in-law, and ask them before using any.
items.quote: 子婦無私貨，無私畜，無私器 — A son and daughter-in-law have no private goods, no private savings, no private utensils.

items.text: Offer every gift you receive to your parents-in-law; if they give it back, refuse; and give anything to your own relatives only with their permission.
items.quote: 婦或賜之...則受而獻諸舅姑 — If a daughter-in-law is given something, she receives it and presents it to her parents-in-law.

items.text: When your father calls, answer at once with a respectful 'yes,' drop what you are doing, and run to him.
items.quote: 父召無諾，唯而起 — When your father calls, do not say 'yes' casually; answer respectfully and rise.

items.text: When your parents are old, do not go to a different place without telling them, and return by the promised time.
items.quote: 親老出不易方，復不過時 — When parents are old, when you go out do not change your destination, and return within the expected time.

items.text: When your parents are ill, set aside your own comforts and pleasures; devote yourself to their care; taste their medicine before giving it.
items.quote: 親有疾飮藥，子先嘗之 — When a parent is ill and takes medicine, the child first tastes it.

items.text: If your parents love you, rejoice and do not forget; if they dislike you, be fearful but not resentful; if they err, remonstrate gently and persistently; even if they beat you, do not resent them.
items.quote: 父母有過，下氣怡色，柔聲以諫 — When parents have faults, with bated breath and pleasant countenance, remonstrate in a gentle voice.

items.text: If your parents are displeased with your wife, send her away; if they approve of her, treat her with full marital respect even if you dislike her.
items.quote: 子甚宜其妻，父母不說出 — If a son is very pleased with his wife but his parents are not pleased, he should divorce her.
items.conflict: Marriage is a covenant before God; parents' approval does not authorize divorce (Mark 10:9).

items.needs_role: all sons (both legitimate and by concubines)
items.text: Revere the lineage heir and his wife; even if you are rich and powerful, do not bring your wealth or entourage into his house, but enter in humility.
items.quote: 適子?庶子祗事宗子?宗婦 — The sons of the main wife and of concubines should respectfully serve the lineage heir and his wife.

items.text: After your father-in-law dies and your mother-in-law retires, as eldest daughter-in-law, ask her about every matter—rites and guests—and do not act on your own.
items.quote: 冡婦所祭祀?賓客，每事必請於姑 — The eldest daughter-in-law must ask her mother-in-law about every matter concerning sacrifices and guests.

items.text: As a younger daughter-in-law, defer to the eldest daughter-in-law; do not compete with her or act as her equal.
items.quote: 不敢竝行，不敢竝命，不敢竝坐 — They dare not walk side by side, give orders together, or sit together.

items.text: For three years after your father's death, do not change his ways; and in all you do, seek to bring him honor and avoid shame.
items.quote: 三年無改於父之道，可謂孝矣 — If for three years he does not change from the way of his father, he may be called filial.

items.text: Both husband and wife must personally perform the ancestral sacrifices; the head must preside; do not sell the sacrificial vessels or cut the trees on the grave mounds.
items.quote: 夫祭也者，必夫婦親之 — In sacrifice, the husband and wife must perform it in person.
items.conflict: Ancestral rites are offerings to the dead, which Scripture forbids (Deut. 18:10-12; 1 Cor. 10:20-21).
